mainTopic: Pregnancy from first relations (תמר, ער and אונן, a כלה's טומאה), the ten-year rule, and שמואל's three-month wait
overview: The amud opens with a challenge to the rule that a woman does not conceive from her first act of relations, since תמר did. The גמרא answers that תמר had already broken her hymen herself. It explains that ער and אונן never had normal relations with her, and it learns from a פסוק that ער acted like אונן. Next comes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about what the word 'אותה' excludes from the טומאה of relations. רב נחמן explains that רבי יהודה exempts a כלה because a woman does not conceive from her first relations. Then רבי יוחנן teaches that a woman who waited ten years before remarrying will not give birth. רב נחמן limits this rule, and two stories back it up. Finally שמואל rules who must wait three months before marrying, and the גמרא works out that his case of a minor בת ישראל is about זנות.

steps.title: Challenge from תמר's first pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a woman does not conceive from a first act of relations, because תמר did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But תמר became pregnant from her very first act of relations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier rule that a woman cannot conceive from a first act of relations. It points to תמר, who conceived from her first time with יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule says a first act of relations does not lead to pregnancy. תמר seems to break that rule, since the פסוק says she conceived from יהודה. If the rule were true, how could this happen?

phrases.english: But Tamar became pregnant from the first act of intercourse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier rule (from before this section) that a woman does not conceive from a first act of relations.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a woman does not conceive from a first act of relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample from the פסוק: תמר conceived from her first time.

steps.title: תמר had already removed her virginity
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that תמר had broken her hymen with her finger beforehand, so this was not truly a 'first' act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: תמר broke her hymen with her finger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תמר's case does not count as a true first time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the woman's physical state, not on who the man is. Since תמר had already broken her hymen herself, her first act of relations worked like a later one, so she could conceive. The rule stays in place.

phrases.english: He said to him: Tamar broke [her hymen] with her finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from תמר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: it was not truly a first act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמר conceived from a true first act, which would break the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her virginity had already been removed, so the rule is not broken.

steps.title: Support from רבי יצחק's nickname 'תמר'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports a nickname that shows a tradition that תמר broke her hymen with her finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: all the women in רבי's household who broke their hymens were called 'תמר.' Why were they called 'תמר'? After תמר, who broke hers with her finger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer it just gave. A known nickname shows that people had a tradition about what תמר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women who did this were nicknamed after תמר, it shows a known tradition that תמר did this herself. That backs up the answer in Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: the household of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מוֹעֹכוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי — תָּמָר שְׁמָן,
phrases.english: All those [women] of the household of Rabbi who broke [their hymens], their name is Tamar,
and why are they called Tamar?
After Tamar, who broke [her hymen] with her finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That תמר broke her hymen with her finger.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's report of the nickname 'תמר' used in בית רבי.

steps.title: What about ער and אונן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why תמר would still have been a virgin at all, since she had been married to ער and אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there were ער and אונן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption that תמר was a virgin when she was with יהודה. She had already been married twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion assumes תמר's time with יהודה was her first. But she had been the wife of ער and then of אונן. If they were with her normally, her time with יהודה was not a 'first' at all, and the story has nothing to do with the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: יהודה's two older sons, תמר's earlier husbands

phrases.english: But weren't there Er and Onan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind Steps 1 to 3 that תמר was a virgin.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that תמר was still a virgin when she was with יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She had two earlier husbands, so she should not have been a virgin.

steps.title: ער and אונן were not with her in the normal way
steps.stepSummary: ער and אונן had relations with תמר only in an unnatural way, so she remained a virgin.
steps.simpleTranslation: ער and אונן had relations in an unnatural way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ער and אונן never had normal relations with תמר, so she was still a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their relations with her were not in the normal way, so her virginity was not affected. That is why her time with יהודה counts as a first act. This also fits why she had to break her hymen herself.

phrases.english: Er and Onan had relations not in the normal manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about ער and אונן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the earlier marriages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ער and אונן had normal relations with her, so she was not a virgin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their relations were unnatural, so she stayed a virgin.

steps.title: A ברייתא compares 'spilling outside' to ער and אונן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a nursing mother compares withdrawing during relations to the act of ער and אונן, which suggests their relations were normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: for all twenty-four months a man has relations normally but spills outside. This is the view of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים said to him: this is just like the act of ער and אונן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge Step 5. The חכמים compare normal relations ending with spilling outside to what ער and אונן did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows a man to withdraw during the 24 months of nursing, so that his wife does not become pregnant. The חכמים reject this as being 'like ער and אונן.' Since the case in the ברייתא is normal relations, the comparison suggests ער and אונן also had normal relations. That would mean תמר was not a virgin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is about ער and אונן themselves. It is about a married couple during nursing. The חכמים only use ער and אונן as a comparison, and the גמרא's question is how far that comparison goes.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: All twenty-four months
phrases.notes: These are the months a baby nurses. A new pregnancy could stop the mother's milk.

phrases.english: he threshes inside and winnows outside,
phrases.notes: This is a farming picture: relations in the normal way, but the seed is spilled outside.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer. They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הַלָּלוּ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּמַעֲשֵׂה עֵר וְאוֹנָן!
phrases.english: These are nothing but like the act of Er and Onan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 5 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ער and אונן had relations only in an unnatural way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים compare normal relations with spilling outside to ער and אונן. That suggests ער and אונן also had normal relations.

steps.title: The comparison is only partial
steps.stepSummary: The act in the ברייתא is like ער and אונן in that seed is wasted, but unlike them in that it is normal relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the act of ער and אונן and also not like it. It is like it in wasting seed, as the פסוק says, 'when he came to his brother's wife, he spilled it on the ground.' It is not like it, because there it was unnatural relations and here it is normal relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים in the ברייתא only meant a partial comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point the two cases share is wasting seed, as the פסוק about אונן shows. They differ in the type of relations: ער and אונן's was unnatural, while the ברייתא's case is normal. So the ברייתא does not prove that ער and אונן had normal relations, and Step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: and he spilled (it) on the ground

steps.whatToRemember: A comparison in a source can match on one point only. The ברייתא compares the case to ער and אונן only in wasting seed, not in the type of relations.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה עֵר וְאוֹנָן, וְלֹא כְּמַעֲשֵׂה עֵר וְאוֹנָן.
phrases.english: Like the act of Er and Onan, and not like the act of Er and Onan.
Like the act of Er and Onan, as it is written:
"And it was, when he came to his brother's wife,
he spilled it on the ground."
And not like the act of Er and Onan,
for there it was not in the normal manner,
while here it is in the normal manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה עֵר וְאוֹנָן, וְלֹא כְּמַעֲשֵׂה עֵר וְאוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 6 by limiting the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison: similar in one way, different in another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's comparison means ער and אונן had normal relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is only about wasting seed. ער and אונן's relations were unnatural.

steps.title: Where do we see that ער did this too?
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק describes אונן's act, but where do we learn that ער did the same?
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand this about אונן, since the פסוק says about him 'he spilled it on the ground.' But how do we know it about ער?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. The פסוק only describes what אונן did, so how do we know ער did the same thing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim in Step 5 covered both brothers. The פסוק about wasting seed is said only about אונן, so ער's behavior still needs a source.

phrases.english: Granted, Onan,
since it is written about him "he spilled it on the ground,"
but Er, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind part of the answer in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ער also wasted seed or had unnatural relations.

steps.title: 'He killed him too': the same death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns from 'וימת גם אותו' that אונן died the same death as ער, so ער must have sinned the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the פסוק says 'and He killed him too.' This means he also died with the same death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the source for ער's act. It comes from the word 'גם' ('too') in the פסוק about אונן's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גם' links אונן's death to ער's death. Same death means the same sin. So the sin the פסוק spells out for אונן was ער's sin as well.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
For it is written: "And He killed him too,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:10. This is said about אונן, after ער had already died.

phrases.english: he too died with that same death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דִּכְתִיב ״וַיָּמֶת גַּם אוֹתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'גם' shows that ער and אונן died the same death, so they committed the same sin.

steps.title: Why would ער do this?
steps.stepSummary: אונן had a reason, since the child would not count as his. What reason did ער have?
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand אונן, because 'the child would not be his.' But ער, why did he act this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about motive. אונן's reason is written in the פסוק, but ער's reason is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אונן was doing יבום, and the child would carry his brother's name, so he had a clear reason. ער was תמר's own first husband, so any child would have been his. Why would he avoid having children?

keyTerms.meaning: the child would not be his

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אוֹנָן, מִשּׁוּם ״לֹּא לוֹ יִהְיֶה הַזָּרַע״,
phrases.english: Granted, Onan, because "the seed would not be his,"

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֵר מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד הָכִי?
phrases.english: but Er, what was the reason he did so?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אוֹנָן, מִשּׁוּם ״לֹּא לוֹ יִהְיֶה הַזָּרַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 9: now that we know ער did this, the גמרא asks why.

steps.title: ער wanted to protect her beauty
steps.stepSummary: ער did not want תמר to become pregnant, because pregnancy would lessen her beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that she would not become pregnant and lose her beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ער's reason: he did not want pregnancy to take away תמר's beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why ער would act this way even though the child would have been his. It also closes this section: ער and אונן both acted to prevent pregnancy, so תמר was still a virgin when she was with יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: תמר's earlier husbands, ער and אונן, never had normal relations with her: אונן because the child would not be his, ער to protect her beauty. So her time with יהודה really was a first, and she was able to conceive only because she had broken her hymen herself.

phrases.english: So that she would not become pregnant and her beauty would lessen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ער avoided pregnancy so that תמר's beauty would not be lessened.

steps.title: A ברייתא: what the word 'אותה' excludes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא argues about what the extra word 'אותה' in the פסוק of טומאת שכבת זרע comes to exclude. רבי יהודה says a כלה, and the חכמים say relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'With her' comes to exclude a bride. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: it excludes relations done in an unusual way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. The ברייתא argues about what the word 'אותה' in the פסוק leaves out from the rule that a woman becomes טמא through relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a woman who has relations with a man becomes טמא. The word 'אותה' (with her) is treated as coming to leave something out. רבי יהודה says it leaves out a כלה, so she does not become טמא. The חכמים say it leaves out relations שלא כדרכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught; this opens a ברייתא
To exclude; this case is left out of the rule
A bride at her first relations after marriage
Relations not done in the normal way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה means a כלה is never טמא in any way. He is only talking about the טומאה a woman gets from relations, and only for this first time.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"With her" comes to exclude a bride,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:18. This is the פסוק about a woman becoming טמא after relations.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say: it excludes relations done in an unusual way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא. It ties in with the earlier topic of relations that cannot lead to pregnancy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: 'אותה' excludes a כלה. חכמים: 'אותה' excludes relations שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה protecting the bride's adornments?
steps.stepSummary: הון בריה דרב נחמן suggests that רבי יהודה exempts a כלה because the Torah did not want to spoil her adornments.
steps.simpleTranslation: הון, son of רב נחמן, said to רב נחמן: Shall we say that רבי יהודה holds that the תורה had mercy on a bride's adornments?
steps.whatsHappening: הון asks his father רב נחמן for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view. He offers one possible reason: the תורה wanted to spare the bride's jewelry and makeup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כלה were טמא, she would have to immerse in a מקוה, and that could ruin her makeup and adornments. הון suggests the תורה exempted her to avoid this. This is a guess at the reason, and the next step will replace it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It offers a possible explanation
A bride's adornments, such as jewelry and makeup

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Hon, son of Rav Nachman, said to Rav Nachman:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yehuda holds
that the Torah had mercy on a bride's adornments?
phrases.notes: The idea is that she would not need to immerse in water and spoil her makeup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יהודה exclude a כלה? Is it to protect her adornments?

steps.title: The reason: no pregnancy from first relations
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבי יהודה's reason is that a woman does not become pregnant from her first relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is because a woman does not become pregnant from the first relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects his son's suggestion and gives a different reason for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of relations with 'שכבת זרע', meaning relations that can lead to a child. Since a woman does not conceive from her first relations, the כלה's first time does not count for this טומאה. So the reason has nothing to do with her adornments. It comes from the nature of the act itself.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a כלה's first relations do not make her טמא, because a woman does not conceive from her first relations.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is because a woman does not become pregnant
from the first relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אִשָּׁה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת מִבִּיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers הון's question with a different reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה exempts the כלה because first relations cannot lead to pregnancy. It is not about protecting her adornments.

steps.title: What exactly do they argue about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real point of disagreement is between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks what the two sides actually argue about, and it will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side uses the word 'אותה' to exclude something different. The question is why. Does each side read the rest of the פסוק differently too?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא to find the root of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying difference in how רבי יהודה and the חכמים read the פסוק?

steps.title: How each side reads the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use 'שכבת זרע' to exclude העראה and 'אותה' to exclude שלא כדרכה. רבי יהודה learns both of those from 'שכבת זרע', which frees 'אותה' to exclude a כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים hold: 'Emission of seed' excludes the first stage of relations, and 'with her' excludes relations in an unusual way. רבי יהודה holds: both unusual relations and the first stage of relations are learned from 'emission of seed', so 'with her' excludes a bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the argument is about how much the words 'שכבת זרע' already teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say 'שכבת זרע' only leaves out העראה, the first stage before completion. So they need 'אותה' to leave out relations שלא כדרכה. רבי יהודה says 'שכבת זרע' means relations that could produce a child, so it already leaves out both cases. That leaves 'אותה' free to teach about a כלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Emission of seed; words from the פסוק
The first stage of relations, without completion
Is derived from; is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to this: does 'שכבת זרע' already leave out relations שלא כדרכה? רבי יהודה says yes, so 'אותה' is free to exclude a כלה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
"Emission of seed" excludes the first stage of relations.
"With her" excludes relations in an unusual way.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
unusual relations and the first stage of relations
are both learned from "emission of seed".
"With her" excludes a bride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the two sides argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about how much 'שכבת זרע' covers. For רבי יהודה it covers both העראה and שלא כדרכה, so 'אותה' can teach about a כלה.

steps.title: A woman who waited ten years will not give birth
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that a woman who waited ten years after her husband and then remarried will no longer give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any woman who waited ten years after her husband and then married will no longer give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on a related topic: a case where a woman cannot become pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of when relations can or cannot lead to pregnancy. רבי יוחנן's rule is that ten years without a husband ends a woman's ability to have children, even after she remarries.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
She will no longer give birth

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Any woman who waited after her husband
phrases.notes: He means after her husband died or divorced her.

phrases.english: ten years and then married
will no longer give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related teaching about when a woman cannot become pregnant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who waited ten years after her husband and then remarried will not have children.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits the rule to a woman who had no plan to remarry
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says רבי יוחנן's rule applies only to a woman who did not plan to remarry. If she did plan to remarry, she can still become pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They taught this only when she did not intend to marry. But if she intended to marry, she can become pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows רבי יוחנן's rule so it covers only one kind of woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule now depends on what the woman was thinking during those years. If she had no plan to remarry, the rule applies. If she always planned to remarry, she can still have children.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of; this limits a rule

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתָּהּ לְהִנָּשֵׂא,
phrases.english: They taught this only when she does not intend to marry,
but if she intends to marry, she can become pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתָּהּ לְהִנָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's rule to one case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's rule applies only if the woman did not intend to remarry.

steps.title: רבא's wife: her mind was on him
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his wife, בת רב חסדא, that the Rabbis are whispering about her. She answers that her mind was set on him, which fits רב נחמן's limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to the daughter of רב חסדא: The Rabbis are whispering about you! She said to him: My mind was on you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב נחמן's limit in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis suspected her because she gave birth even though she had waited a long time before marrying רבא. Her answer shows that she always intended to marry him. By רב נחמן's limit, a woman who intends to marry can still become pregnant, so there is nothing to suspect.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְבַת רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rava said to the daughter of Rav Chisda:
The Rabbis are whispering about you!
She said to him:
My mind was on you.
phrases.notes: She means she always planned to marry him, so רב נחמן's limit fits her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְבַת רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows רב נחמן's limit at work.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that a woman who intends to remarry can still become pregnant
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבא's wife, whose mind was set on marrying him

steps.title: The woman before רב יוסף confesses
steps.stepSummary: A woman claims she waited ten years and still gave birth. רב יוסף tells her not to cast doubt on the Sages, and she admits she had relations with a non-Jew during those years.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רב יוסף and said: My teacher, I waited ten years after my husband and gave birth! He said to her: My daughter, do not speak badly of the words of the Sages! She said to him: I had relations with a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the ten-year topic with a story in which רבי יוחנן's rule seems to be broken, but it turns out the rule still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her claim seemed to go against רבי יוחנן's rule. Her confession shows she did not really wait ten years without relations. So the rule stands, and רב יוסף was right to defend it.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him; in front of him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ten-year rule stands, with רב נחמן's limit: it does not apply to a woman who intended to remarry. A case that seems to break the rule really did not.

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rav Yosef,
said to him: My teacher,
I waited after my husband
phrases.notes: Some versions have אנא, in round brackets, and the corrected wording has אני, in square brackets. Both just mean 'I'.

phrases.english: ten years, and I gave birth!
He said to her: My daughter,

phrases.aramaic: אַל תּוֹצִיאִי לַעַז עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים!
phrases.english: do not speak badly of the words of the Sages!
She said to him: I had relations with a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story. This one upholds רבי יוחנן's main rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that a woman who waited ten years will not give birth
steps.raayaSupportSource: The woman's confession that she had not really gone ten years without relations

steps.title: שמואל: Everyone waits three months, except a minor convert and a minor freed maidservant
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that all women who had relations must wait three months. A minor גיורת and a minor משוחררת are exempt, but a minor בת ישראל must wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: All these women must wait three months before marrying, except a convert who is a minor and a freed maidservant who is a minor. But a minor girl who is a בת ישראל must wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל about which women must wait three months before marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-month wait exists so that if a baby is born, we know which man is the father. שמואל exempts a minor convert and a minor freed maidservant. He then stresses that a Jewish-born minor is not exempt, and must wait like anyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: To wait three months before marrying, so that we can tell whose child a baby is
A girl who is a minor

steps.confusionAlert: The word קטנה applies to both exceptions. Only a MINOR convert or freed maidservant is exempt, not an adult one.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
And all of them must wait three months,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all women who had relations and so might be pregnant.

phrases.english: except for a minor convert and a minor freed maidservant.
But a minor Jewish-born girl
must wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְכוּלָּן צְרִיכוֹת לְהַמְתִּין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the stories about waiting ten years (Steps 17-20).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All women who had relations wait three months. A minor convert and a minor freed maidservant are exempt. A minor בת ישראל is not exempt.

steps.title: Which case of a minor Jewish girl does שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation שמואל's rule about a minor בת ישראל is talking about. It rules out מיאון and גט, using another statement of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what case is he speaking? If she left her marriage through מיאון, didn't שמואל say she does not need to wait? And if she left through a גט, שמואל already said that once! For שמואל said: If she refused him, she does not need to wait three months. If he gave her a גט, she must wait three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case of a minor Jewish girl שמואל means, and knocks out the two obvious options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון cannot be the case, because שמואל himself said that a girl who leaves by refusal does not wait. A גט also cannot be the case, because שמואל already taught that, so he would not need to say it again. This leaves the גמרא looking for a third case.

keyTerms.meaning: "And in what case?": a question asking which situation a rule is talking about
Refusal: a minor girl married off by her mother or brothers can reject the marriage
One time: he already said this once

phrases.english: And in what case?
If she left the marriage through refusal,
but didn't Shmuel say that she does not need to wait?
And if she left through a bill of divorce,
didn't Shmuel already say it one time?
For Shmuel said:
If she refused him,
she does not need to wait three months;
if he gave her a bill of divorce,
she must wait three months!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case step 21's rule about a minor בת ישראל is talking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation of a minor Jewish girl requires the three-month wait in שמואל's rule, given that מיאון and גט are both ruled out by his other statement?
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible readings of שמואל's rule as being about מיאון or גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מיאון would contradict שמואל's own ruling, and a גט would make his statement a needless repeat.

steps.title: Answer: שמואל means a minor who had relations through זנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל's rule is about a minor בת ישראל who had relations outside of marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means a minor who had relations through זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. שמואל was talking about a minor Jewish girl who had relations outside of marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מיאון and גט were both ruled out, only a case with no marriage at all is left. This means שמואל's statement teaches something new: even a minor who had relations through זנות must wait three months.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather": shows the גמרא is moving to the only remaining option

phrases.english: Rather, he means through promiscuous relations,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by choosing the remaining option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule about a minor בת ישראל is about a case of זנות.
